quests.question: He talked about the trip ___ he had already been there.
quests.hint: His way of talking suggests something that may not be true.
quests.explanation: 'As if' introduces a comparison to an imagined situation — he spoke as though he had prior experience.

quests.question: The town hall meeting was moved online ___ so many people wanted to attend.
quests.hint: High interest explains the format change.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the reason for a decision — strong interest led to moving the meeting online.

quests.question: The old library needed repairs, ___ the town organized a fundraiser.
quests.hint: A specific need directly led to a community response.
quests.explanation: 'So' introduces a result — the need for repairs led to the fundraiser.

quests.question: ___ the flight was fully booked, we managed to get seats together.
quests.hint: A difficult situation is acknowledged, but the outcome was still favorable.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' introduces a strong concession — despite a full flight, seats together were still found.

quests.question: You can bring one carry-on bag ___ it fits under the seat.
quests.hint: Fitting under the seat is the specific rule attached to the bag.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' means 'on the condition that' — bringing the bag depends on this size requirement.

quests.question: Check the visa requirements ___ you book your flights.
quests.hint: One step should always come ahead of the booking.
quests.explanation: 'Before' places checking requirements earlier in time than booking.

quests.question: ___ the app ___ the website crashed during the product launch.
quests.hint: Two platforms failed together, at the same time.
quests.explanation: 'Both...and' includes two items together — the app and the website both crashed.

quests.question: Customer complaints increased ___ the new update slowed the app down.
quests.hint: A technical change explains the rise in complaints.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a result — the slow update caused more complaints.

quests.question: Developers released a patch ___ the bug would be fixed quickly.
quests.hint: Releasing the patch has one clear, intended goal.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces a purpose — the patch was released to fix the bug.

quests.question: She moved ___ every step caused her pain.
quests.hint: Her movement suggests a feeling without stating it directly.
quests.explanation: 'As if' introduces a comparison — her way of moving suggested pain, whether or not it was confirmed.

quests.question: ___ the treatment is expensive, most patients say it's worth it.
quests.hint: A real drawback is acknowledged, but opinions stay positive.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' introduces a strong concession — despite the cost, patients still value the treatment.

quests.question: The waiting room was full, ___ the appointment still started on time.
quests.hint: A crowded room didn't affect the schedule.
quests.explanation: 'But' introduces a contrast — a full waiting room didn't cause a delay.

quests.question: ___ the credits start rolling, most people leave their seats.
quests.hint: The credits starting is the trigger for people to get up.
quests.explanation: 'Once' means 'as soon as this begins' — the credits starting is what prompts people to leave.

quests.question: You can bring snacks into the theater, ___ they're not noisy to unwrap.
quests.hint: Being quiet to open is the specific rule attached to bringing snacks.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' means 'on the condition that' — bringing snacks depends on this one rule.

quests.question: The show was postponed ___ the lead actor lost his voice.
quests.hint: A specific health issue explains the postponement.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the reason for a decision — losing his voice caused the postponement.

quests.question: The lecture was ___ long that half the students left early.
quests.hint: This word pairs directly with an adjective, not with a noun.
quests.explanation: 'So' combines with an adjective before a 'that' result clause — the degree of length caused the result.

quests.question: It was ___ a long lecture that half the students left early.
quests.hint: This word pairs directly with a noun phrase, unlike its close relative.
quests.explanation: 'Such' combines with a noun phrase before a 'that' result clause — the degree of the lecture caused the result.

quests.question: I tried on the jacket ___ decided it was perfect.
quests.hint: Two actions happened right after each other in the same visit.
quests.explanation: 'And' links two actions in sequence — trying on and deciding happened one after the other.

quests.question: You can submit the form online, ___ you can mail it to our office.
quests.hint: Two submission methods are offered — only one is needed.
quests.explanation: 'Or' presents two alternatives — either method of submitting the form works.

quests.question: ___ remote work has benefits, some employees miss the office atmosphere.
quests.hint: Real advantages are acknowledged, but something else is still missed.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' introduces a strong concession — despite the benefits, the office atmosphere is still missed.

quests.question: Your request will be approved ___ you submit it two weeks in advance.
quests.hint: Submitting two weeks early is the specific requirement here.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' means 'on the condition that' — approval depends on this exact timing.

quests.question: My parents moved closer to us ___ they wanted to see the grandchildren more often.
quests.hint: A specific wish explains the decision to move.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the reason for a decision — wanting more time with grandchildren caused the move.

quests.question: The whole family caught the flu, ___ we cancelled the reunion.
quests.hint: Illness directly led to a change of plans.
quests.explanation: 'So' introduces a result — the flu caused the reunion to be cancelled.

quests.question: ___ the drive to my parents' house takes six hours, we visit every summer.
quests.hint: A real inconvenience is acknowledged, but it doesn't stop the visits.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concession — despite the long drive, the visits still happen every year.

quests.question: The new park is not only beautiful ___ also home to several rare birds.
quests.hint: 'Not only' always pairs with one word to add a second impressive fact.
quests.explanation: 'Not only...but also' adds a second impressive quality — beauty and rare wildlife.

quests.question: The factory installed filters ___ less smoke would enter the air.
quests.hint: Installing filters has one clear, intended goal.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces a purpose — the filters were installed to reduce smoke in the air.

quests.question: ___ the river is cleaned up, local fish populations should recover.
quests.hint: Cleaning the river is the trigger for the next positive change.
quests.explanation: 'Once' means 'as soon as this is complete' — the cleanup is what allows recovery to begin.

quests.question: ___ ticket prices went up, the stadium was still completely full.
quests.hint: A real downside is acknowledged, but attendance stayed strong.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' introduces a strong concession — despite higher prices, the stadium still sold out.

quests.question: The instructions were in a foreign language, ___ the diagrams made assembly easy.
quests.hint: One challenge is balanced by something that made the task manageable.
quests.explanation: 'But' introduces a contrast — a language barrier was offset by clear diagrams.

quests.question: You'll pass the driving test ___ you stay calm and follow the checklist.
quests.hint: Staying calm and following steps is the condition for passing.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' means 'on the condition that' — passing the test depends on this behavior.
